Republic of Sereleia: Visitor Frequently Asked Questions
Evaluation corpus edition. Sereleia is a fictional island nation; every answer below is invented for retrieval testing.

Q: Where is Sereleia and how do I get there?
A: Sereleia is an archipelago in the North Atlantic, roughly 800 kilometres west of Ireland. The only international airport is Althaven Vestera Airport on the main island of Vestera. Direct flights operate from Dublin, Reykjavik and Halifax; the Dublin flight takes about two hours and forty minutes. A weekly ferry from Galway carries vehicles and takes eighteen hours.

Q: Do I need a visa?
A: Citizens of the European Union, the United Kingdom, Canada and the United States may visit for up to 90 days without a visa. Other nationals apply online through the Sereleian Consular Portal; standard processing takes ten working days and the fee is 45 sereleian crowns.

Q: What currency is used and can I pay by card?
A: The currency is the sereleian crown, subdivided into 100 pence. Cards are accepted almost everywhere on Vestera and Ostera, but many family guesthouses on Sydra only take cash. Automated teller machines are available in Althaven, Port Ostera and the Sydra ferry terminal.

Q: When is the best time to visit?
A: The climate is temperate maritime. June to September offers the longest days and the calmest seas; the annual Lantern Tide festival is held on the first weekend of August. Winter visits are popular with geothermal spa travellers, since the Ostera hot springs stay at 38 degrees Celsius all year.

Q: How do I travel between the islands?
A: The public ferry network links the three main islands. The Vestera to Ostera crossing takes 50 minutes and runs six times a day; the Vestera to Sydra crossing takes two hours and runs twice a day in summer and once a day in winter. Inter-island flights are not available; the Sydra biodiversity reserve prohibits aircraft below 3,000 metres.

Q: Is the tap water safe and what about the geothermal pools?
A: Tap water is safe to drink on all three islands. Geothermal pools on Ostera are managed by the Ostera Springs Trust; visitors must shower before entering and children under six are not admitted to the hottest pool, which is kept at 42 degrees Celsius.

Q: What are the rules in the Sydra biodiversity reserve?
A: Visitors must stay on marked trails, may not bring pets, and must carry all waste out of the reserve. Guided walks are limited to twelve people. Drones are banned throughout the reserve, and the reserve authority fines violations up to 2,000 crowns.

Q: Which language is spoken?
A: The official language is Sereleian, a Celtic language with Norse loanwords. English is taught from primary school and is spoken fluently by most residents under sixty. Road signs are bilingual on Vestera and Ostera and Sereleian-only on Sydra.

Q: How does the government work and can visitors attend council sessions?
A: Sereleia is a Consensus Republic without political parties. The Grand Council of 300 representatives meets in Althaven, and its public gallery admits visitors on Tuesdays and Thursdays with a free ticket collected from the council office. Representatives serve a single four-year term.

Q: What emergency numbers should I know?
A: Dial 112 for police, fire and medical emergencies anywhere in Sereleia. The coastguard can be reached on 116 from any phone. The Althaven General Hospital is the only hospital with a 24-hour emergency department; Ostera and Sydra have clinics that close at 20:00.

Q: Are there restrictions on bringing food or plants?
A: Fresh fruit, seeds, live plants and soil may not be brought into Sereleia because of the Sydra reserve's biosecurity rules. Packaged food is allowed. Declare any hiking equipment used abroad in the last month so it can be cleaned at the arrivals hall.

Q: How expensive is a typical trip?
A: A mid-range guesthouse costs 120 to 180 crowns per night. A ferry ticket between Vestera and Ostera costs 14 crowns, and a day pass on the Althaven tram network costs 6 crowns. Restaurants add a service charge of 10 percent; further tipping is not expected.
